newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo river shipper sees 50 pct rise in 1997 cargo.
newsitem.headline: Yugo river shipper sees 50 pct rise in 1997 cargo.

text.p: BELGRADE, May 29 (Tanjug) - Yugoslav river shipping company Jugoslovensko Recno Brodarstvo (JRB) expects to transport 2.5 million tonnes of goods in 1997, up 50 percent on the previous year, Tanjug news agency reported on Thursday.
JRB will transport some two million tonnes of liquid cargos and 500,000 tonnes of coke, lime and other goods, the agency quoted JRB director Dusan Strugar as saying.
At the moment the shipper is operating with 65 percent capacity and is trying to speed up overhaul of the remaining ships and secure new deals.
This is the first year of normal operation of the company after several years of sanctions imposed on Yugoslavia in May 1992 and lifted last October.
JRB lost 95 percent of its market and suffered a loss of 100 million dinars ($17.6 million) because of the sanctions, Strugar said. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4305
